title: Jamaican beef patties
skill: A turmeric pastry, filled and crimped

move.title: Golden pastry, a spiced filling
move.body: Beef patties are Jamaica's street food: half-moons of flaky, turmeric-gold pastry around a spiced beef filling with thyme, allspice, and Scotch bonnet. You'll make the pastry with butter, cook and thicken the filling, then fill, crimp, and bake them golden.

callback.body: Empanadas fold a butter pastry around a cooked beef filling, too. Jamaican patties color the pastry with turmeric and curry powder, and thicken the filling with breadcrumbs so it stays moist without leaking.

why.title: Turmeric in the pastry
why.body: Turmeric and curry powder rubbed into the flour give the crust its famous yellow color and a little warmth. Many Jamaican bakeries use beef fat in it; this one uses butter.

why.title: Thyme, allspice, and Scotch bonnet
why.body: These three are the base of Jamaican cooking. Allspice, called pimento in Jamaica, tastes like cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg together. Scotch bonnet brings fruity heat.

why.title: Breadcrumbs in the filling
why.body: Simmered with broth, breadcrumbs soak it up and turn the filling thick and moist, so it doesn't run out of the pastry.

why.title: Chill before baking
why.body: Shaping warms the butter. Fifteen minutes in the fridge firms it so the pastry bakes flaky.

wrong.fix: Simmer it a few minutes longer, until the spoon leaves a trail.

wrong.sign: The pastry cracks when you fold it
wrong.fix: It's too cold. Let it sit 5 minutes.
There was filling on the edge. Keep it in the middle and crimp firmly.
Use only half the Scotch bonnet, with no seeds, next time.

quiz.q: What gives the pastry its yellow color?
What is allspice called in Jamaica?
quiz.explain: It tastes like cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg.

quiz.q: What should the filling read after baking?

substitutions.note: Milder. Use a whole one, seeded.

steps.text: Weigh the flour into the large bowl with the turmeric, curry powder, and salt. Cut in the cold butter to pea size, then toss in ice water a tablespoon at a time until a squeezed handful holds.
steps.look: Bright yellow crumbs that hold when squeezed.

steps.text: Press into a disk, wrap, and chill.
Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and slice the green onions. Seed and mince the Scotch bonnet, then wash your hands well before touching your face.
Soften the onion in the oil in the skillet over medium heat, then add the garlic, green onion, and Scotch bonnet for 1 minute.
Add the beef and the spices and brown it, breaking it up.
Discard the package and wash your hands.
Stir in the broth and panko and simmer until thick and moist. Spread on the plate to cool.
steps.look: The spoon leaves a trail that stays.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan.
Roll the pastry ⅛ inch thick and cut eight 6-inch rounds around a bowl, rerolling the scraps once.
Spoon filling onto half of each round, wet the edge, fold, press out the air, and crimp with the fork. Set on the pan and chill.

steps.look: Deep golden yellow, flaky at the edges.

steps.text: Check the filling of one patty through the side: 165°F.
Cool a few minutes on the rack.
